name: China Masters
stakes: This Super 750 event offers India's contingent a vital opportunity to gather crucial ranking points and build momentum as the season progresses.
summary: India's top shuttlers head to Shenzhen for the China Masters, a crucial Super 750 event following the World Championships. Men's Doubles pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, seeded 5th, will be looking to build on their Worlds quarterfinal run, though fitness concerns have been a recurring theme. The spotlight also falls on PV Sindhu, who seeks a strong rebound after an earlier-than-expected exit at the Worlds. Lakshya Sen, another key Men's Singles contender, is aiming for a deep run to regain momentum. Meanwhile, the Women's Doubles duo of Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand arrive with significant confidence, fresh off their historic World Championships bronze medal—a performance that signals their top form and rising stature. India's top Mixed Doubles pair, Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto, continue their ascent and will be eager to make their mark. Veteran HS Prannoy and young Malvika Bansod complete the contingent, both seeking valuable tour experience and strong performances in a highly competitive field.
